sectors.name: Technology

Cross-market divergence favors US tech beta over IDX tech, but selective Indonesian plays offer higher alpha as foreign inflows return post-election stability.
sectors.ai: Accumulate US-listed AI-infrastructure names (NBIS, COHR, LITE) on pullbacks; Indonesia tech remains a laggard—overweight CRWV and 035420 for domestic AI-cloud and data-center exposure, but keep ID allocation under 15% until rupiah stabilizes. Trim ORCL into strength; rotate into pure-play optical/network names with earnings momentum.

sectors.name: Mining & Energy
themes: Domestic Indonesian demand and infrastructure spending remain a durable driver for coal and energy names, insulating them from US cyclical weakness.
Nickel and downstream processing (MDKA, MBMA, INCO) benefit from long-term EV battery supply-chain localization policies, despite global price volatility.
The ID/US rate differential and rupiah stability create a structural tailwind for local-currency commodity producers, amplifying earnings when USD softens.
sectors.ai: Buy selective exposure to Indonesian coal and nickel names on the back of strong ID demand and a weak USD tailwind, but stay nimble given WATCH signal. Favor INDY, ADMR, and INCO for volume and margin leverage; avoid chasing ALKA/BAJA speculative spikes. Trim into strength if IDX momentum fades, as US softness caps global risk appetite.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: US IRA and tariff clarity are restoring margins for domestic solar manufacturers, making FSLR and SEDG structural winners as module demand reaccelerates into 2025.
Indonesia's nickel and EV battery integration is pulling downstream climate-tech capital, with TOBA and VKTR positioned to monetize the country's resource-to-grid value chain.
Distributed generation and storage software (RUN, ENPH) are compounding as grid bottlenecks and electrification force residential and C&I customers to self-supply, a durable demand shift.
sectors.ai: Buy pullbacks in US-listed solar equipment (FSLR, SEDG, ARRY) and Indonesian electrification plays (TOBA, VKTR) as policy tailwinds and tariff clarity drive repricing. Near-term momentum is strong but crowded; add on 3-5% dips, trim VST into strength. Watch for Q3 earnings confirmation before chasing further upside.

sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG
themes: Small-cap FMCG names are outperforming due to domestic retail investor flows chasing low-float, high-beta stories, a trend likely to persist while liquidity remains ample.
IDR depreciation is a durable tailwind for FMCG exporters like ESTI and MERI, boosting competitiveness and margins, unlike import-reliant peers.
Structural shift toward premiumization and health-conscious products continues to drive demand for higher-margin SKUs, benefiting agile mid-tier players over legacy giants.
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names on momentum, but rotate out of crowded large caps. ENZO, PADA, and MBTO show strong volume-backed rallies; chase only with tight stops. Prefer exporters (ESTI, MERI) for IDR weakness tailwind. Trim AGAR into strength. Overall, stay underweight sector until earnings confirm margin recovery.

State-linked energy infrastructure (RGAS, MIRA) is benefiting from gas monetization policy shifts, yet execution risk and thin liquidity cap upside relative to pure-play construction names.
sectors.ai: Buy the infrastructure re-rating: TALF/BRNA/KETR lead a broad ID/US bid on capex visibility, but chase only names with confirmed order books (TALF, KETR) and avoid speculative RGAS/MIRA. Trim AXON/BLDR into strength—US data-center demand is priced in. Add exposure via KETR on pullbacks; sector momentum stays positive into Q3 earnings.

themes: US minimally invasive surgery and robotic platforms (ISRG, SYK) are structurally compounding via procedure volume growth and hospital capex recovery, independent of rate cuts.
Continuous glucose monitoring (DXCM) benefits from expanding reimbursement and diabetes prevalence, a durable demand curve across US and emerging markets.
Indonesian healthcare remains fragmented and policy-sensitive; PRDL's surge reflects speculative distribution gains, not fundamentals, warranting caution despite sector-wide watch signal.

Favor US large-cap device names over IDX laggards; add on any 3-5% pullback, as earnings revisions and M&A flows sustain momentum into Q3.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's ongoing infrastructure spending on ports and toll roads directly boosts logistics efficiency and capacity, creating durable tailwinds for listed operators.
E-commerce penetration growth in secondary cities drives demand for last-mile delivery and cold-chain logistics, structurally lifting volume for mid-cap players.
Government push for downstream processing and export diversification increases inter-island freight movement, benefiting shipping and trucking firms long-term.

Prioritize GTSI and SOCI for momentum continuation, but lock gains into SHIP and TAMU as defensive plays. Watch for pullback in HUMI and SDMU before adding. Overall, maintain overweight with a trailing stop at +0.5% aggregate.

sectors.name: Property & Real Estate

Favor names with recurring income (BKDP, MPRO) over pure speculatives; trim ELTY into strength. Watch for policy catalysts from the new government's housing push.

sectors.name: Crypto & Digital Assets
themes: Indonesia's crypto adoption is structurally tied to remittance and cross-border payment corridors, favoring scalable layer-1s like Stellar and Algorand over speculative tokens.
Regulatory clarity under Bappebti and the upcoming OJK transition will increasingly reward compliant, utility-driven assets, compressing meme-coin premiums.
Global institutional staking flows into proof-of-stake networks (ATOM, AVAX, ADA) are a durable driver, as yield demand outpaces retail trading volume in emerging markets.
sectors.ai: Rotate into layer-1s with proven staking yield and Indonesia-accessible liquidity—ALGO, ATOM, AVAX lead momentum and offer real on-chain activity versus meme-driven pumps. Take partial profits on PUMP and HYPE, which are sentiment-exposed and vulnerable to local exchange listing gaps. Rebalance toward ADA and DOT for relative safety, and watch for a pullback to add AVAX below $30.
